idiom_name: tagged stop message on a worker/queue channel; stream close
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no closable userland queue, so worker pools hand-roll the pill as a distinguishable message object (for example { type: 'stop' }) that each consumer checks and returns from - identity-based sentinels such as a Symbol do not survive structured clone across postMessage. Streams already have the absorbed form: ReadableStreamDefaultController.close() and Node's push(null)/end() deliver the buffered chunks first and then signal EOF to every reader, the same drain-then-stop contract without an in-band sentinel. AbortController and AbortSignal are the harder cancellation channel for a consumer that is blocked and cannot check messages, because a worker stuck in synchronous code never reaches its message handler.
pitfalls: Symbols and object identity do not survive structured clone (postMessage/worker_threads): the pill must be recognised by a serialisable tag, not by identity.
One stop message posted to a MessagePort is consumed by exactly one receiver; a worker pool needs one per worker, or a BroadcastChannel/close protocol.
A worker blocked in synchronous code never reaches its message handler, so the pill cannot interrupt it - use terminate()/AbortSignal for hard stops.
For streams, close()/end() drain buffered chunks and then complete readers, while cancel() discards the buffer: the same pipeline has two very different teardown semantics.
